name: armorpaint
one_liner: Free, open-source software for painting realistic textures onto 3D models — the kind of paint job that makes a game character's armor look scratched, rusty, or worn.
buyer: An indie game studio or freelance 3D artist who needs professional texture-painting tools but can't justify a Substance Painter subscription.
business_use_cases: A freelance 3D artist uses it (paying for the compiled binary) to deliver texture work to indie game clients at a lower cost basis than commercial tools.
A game-asset marketplace seller creates and sells texture packs made with it, undercutting competitors who priced in expensive software licenses.
An art school teaches texturing fundamentals with it since students can use it for free while learning industry-relevant workflows.

money_ideas.idea: The project already sells compiled binaries directly to fund development — a proven, working model.
Sell premade texture/material packs built with the tool on asset marketplaces.

steal_this: Use it to batch-produce a themed texture pack (e.g. 'sci-fi armor materials') this weekend and list it on a game-asset marketplace.
